definition: Monotonous means unchanging and repetitious to the point of being dull.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word monotonous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know monotonous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The hold music is monotonous — the same eight bars looping, softly, for as long as you can stand to wait.
Unvaried just states the fact of no change; monotonous adds the ache — the sameness has started to bore.
Mind-numbing goes past monotonous: the sameness is so total it blanks thought altogether.

One-note is the informal jab for a performance or argument stuck on a single idea, as if a musician played the same note all night. It mocks a lack of range. Monotonous is the broader, more formal complaint that sameness of any kind — a sound, a menu, a routine — has turned dull.

Unvarying states the sameness flatly, as a plain fact with no complaint attached: an unvarying bedtime, an unvarying gray sky. Monotonous adds the verdict that the sameness bores. A surgeon wants an unvarying pulse on the monitor; nobody wants a monotonous one — the word itself carries the groan.

The summer Jonah turned sixteen, he took a job in the exit booth of a downtown parking garage.
At first the novelty carried him: the gate arm, the till, the little sliding window, the ceremony of making change.
By July the shift had gone monotonous — the same three questions from drivers, the same beep of the scanner, hour after hour, until he started counting ceiling tiles to stay awake.
His sister worked the aquarium's ticket desk, just as repetitive on paper, but she swore it never wore on her.
'Different faces every minute,' she said.
That, Jonah decided, was the whole difference.
Repetition alone was survivable; it was repetition with nothing new inside it that ground him down.
